name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.finiteDimensional_space_of_singleton
title: A unital singleton model acts in finite dimension

content.display_title: A unital singleton model acts in finite dimension
content.one_sentence_role: Uses simplicity to put the identity operator in the compact image ideal.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a nonzero irreducible unital $*$-representation. Assume every nonzero irreducible unital $*$-representation of $A$ is unitarily equivalent to $\pi$. Then $H$ is finite dimensional over $\mathbb C$.
content.assumptions: The uniqueness-of-class condition is essential to the argument; mere irreducibility is not asserted to force finite dimension. Separability is assumed for $H$, not for $A$.
content.conclusion: The representation space has a finite complex basis.
content.proof_summary: Obtain faithfulness and simplicity, find a nonzero compact image, and use the resulting nonzero closed ideal to make the identity compact.
proof_steps: Apply [Faithfulness of a unital singleton representation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/Faithful.lean#L67-L108) to the given nonzero ordered unital $A$ and singleton $\pi$ to obtain injectivity. Then [Simplicity from a faithful singleton model](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/Singleton.lean#L29-L55) applies with that injectivity and shows that every closed two-sided ideal of $A$ is $0$ or $A$.

Use [A scalar-corner projection in the unital algebra](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/MinimalProjection.lean#L67-L91) with this singleton representation on separable $H$ to obtain a nonzero projection $p\in A$ with $pap\in\mathbb Cp$ for every $a\in A$. Injectivity gives $\pi(p)\ne0$. Irreducibility, this nonzero image, and the scalar-corner equations are precisely the inputs of [A nonzero represented scalar corner is compact](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/RankOneProjection.lean#L98-L110), whose output is compactness of $\pi(p)$.

Let $I=\{a\in A:\pi(a)\text{ is compact}\}$, the two-sided ideal of [The compact-preimage ideal](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CompactPreimage.lean#L28-L63). It is norm closed by [Closedness of the compact-preimage ideal](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CompactPreimage.lean#L72-L92). Since $p\in I$ and $p\ne0$, $I\ne0$; simplicity therefore forces $I=A$. In particular $1_A\in I$.

By the definition of $I$, $\pi(1_A)$ is compact. Unitality now matters: $$\pi(1_A)=I_H\in\mathcal K(H).$$ The [Compact-identity criterion applied to the same H](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/FiniteDimension.lean#L24-L66) gives $\dim_{\mathbb C}H<\infty$, as used in the final source step.
